rows.subject: argument validation: retry_failed boolean, partition/operation names, request_id, canonicalize, and their order
rows.finding: Current order = partition → operation → retry flag → request ID allocation/validation → input canonicalization → clock/lease allocation. M3.3 submission must retain scope/input validation but expose neither retry_failed nor caller request_id; pin its own exact precedence before source/ledger work.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:574-590; numbered source read shows every validator and the first stateful calls in order.

rows.subject: request-row idempotency lookup and ConflictError when a request_id is rebound to different content
rows.finding: Lookup gives partition-local replay plus immutable operation/input binding; mismatch raises exact ConflictError before revision/status handling. M3.3 private v2 plumbing must allocate a fresh opaque request row, never expose replay or imply proposal deduplication; caller owns attempt identity/content binding.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:592-603; SELECT and three-field comparison precede every existing-request branch.

rows.subject: stale-revision short circuit through _request_revision_is_current
rows.finding: Existing stale requests bypass reclaim/retry and project ReconciliationRequired through _outcome. That cached-request reconciliation guarantee has no M3.3 submission referent; caller owns stale effects, while H14 separately preserves the source-generation revision race guard.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:604-605 and 879-891; helper result immediately routes the persisted row into lifecycle projection.

rows.subject: expired-lease takeover of a `generating` request
rows.finding: Expired generating rows atomically replace lease owner/deadline, increment attempts, and continue at the stored revision. M3.3 submission intentionally provides no concurrent-attempt suppression, crash recovery, takeover, or stale-worker lease fencing; caller owns all four.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:606-616; guarded UPDATE and stored-revision reuse encode the complete takeover guarantee.

rows.subject: retry_failed re-arm of a `failed` request
rows.finding: retry_failed clears the durable error, reacquires a lease, increments attempts, and retries at the stored revision; false replays FallbackFailed. M3.3 source errors are immediate normalized exceptions with zero row/event, so retry/backoff/attempt history moves wholly to caller.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:617-629 and 1004-1005; guarded re-arm contrasts with failed-status replay.

rows.subject: operation registration lookup and NotFoundError
rows.finding: New routes load the exact partition/name row, reject absence with public NotFoundError, and capture its revision. Both M3.3 submission forms need this guarantee; source-backed submission must complete it before invoking the source, then recheck revision before persistence.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:631-637; operation lookup, exact error text, and revision extraction are contiguous.

rows.subject: promoted-artifact exact lookup at the current operation revision
rows.finding: Legacy handle searches one promoted artifact by partition/operation/current revision/input digest. M3.2b already replaced this with full-function System.resolve; explicit M3.3 submission must not resolve first or suppress a caller-requested proposal, and legacy lookup remains until handle deletion.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:638-645 plus .agent/decisions/m3u2b-contract.md sections 1-3 define the shipped resolver replacement.

rows.subject: ambiguity quarantine: suspend every duplicate and emit artifact.ambiguity_quarantined
rows.finding: Legacy handle turns duplicate exact matches into a mutating quarantine: suspend every row, clear promotion hashes, emit one ordered event, then force fallback. M3.3 submission has no artifact-selection responsibility; this path stays byte-stable until the later handle removal.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:646-664; executemany mutation, event payload, and artifacts=[] force are one branch.

rows.subject: _validate_promoted integrity check and artifact.integrity_quarantined quarantine
rows.finding: Legacy handle parses, validates, and executes one artifact; IntegrityError/ValidationError suspends it, clears promotion identity, emits artifact.integrity_quarantined, then falls through to source generation. M3.3 must neither call nor reproduce this mutating resolution path.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:665-695; try/except binds validation and execution failure to quarantine plus fallback.

rows.subject: hit path: INSERT a `resolved` request row and emit request.resolved_by_artifact
rows.finding: A matched artifact canonicalizes output, persists a resolved request cache, emits request.resolved_by_artifact, and returns request-bound Resolved. M3.2b System.resolve already supplies request-free hit/miss with zero write/event; M3.3 adds submission only, so legacy cache/event removal waits.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:696-734 and .agent/decisions/m3u2b-contract.md section 5 pin the legacy/new purity contrast.

rows.subject: miss path: INSERT a `generating` request row holding a lease
rows.finding: Legacy miss reserves generation before source invocation. Unchanged v2 forces M3.3 to keep a private request row, but it can be born directly as pending with proposal_id set and both lease columns NULL; no pre-source row, lease, attempt, or observable request identity is needed.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:735-754; src/cement_runtime/store.py:64-67,108-109 admit pending plumbing and require it for proposal FK.

rows.subject: absent candidate_source becomes _fail_generation('candidate_source_unavailable')
rows.finding: No configured source currently becomes durable failed request state plus fallback_failed event/result. M3.3 source-backed submission must instead raise CandidateSourceError with one contract-published exact message before any request/proposal/event write; direct submission remains usable without a configured source.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:756-757 and 846-878 show absence routed into the same mutating failure helper.

rows.subject: source invocation outside every transaction, with CandidateSourceError and bare Exception both normalized to candidate_source_error
rows.finding: Source invocation and returned candidate/provenance validation occur after reservation transaction exit; CandidateSourceError and every Exception collapse to one stored code, hiding detail. M3.3 must preserve the zero-open-transaction call, normalize both to identical public CandidateSourceError text, and leave zero durable footprint.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:758-776 follows transaction exit at line 754; both except arms call identical failure code.

rows.subject: post-generation re-read: terminal status, stale revision, lease-owner fencing
rows.finding: Second write transaction fences missing/reclaimed reservations and converts revision drift into durable failure. With no pre-source request row, M3.3 needs only an exact operation-revision re-read under the proposal write lock; mismatch must raise the ruled public error and roll back every row/event. Caller owns duplicate-worker fencing.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:778-806; .agent/decisions/m3-map-c-lifecycle.md S7 fork 5 isolates revision recheck from lease ownership.

rows.subject: proposal write: proposal.created event, INSERT proposals, UPDATE request to `pending`, return ReviewRequired
rows.finding: Success atomically emits proposal.created, inserts canonical candidate/provenance, binds pending request, and returns proposal identity plus request identity. M3.3 must share this footprint across direct/source-backed calls, insert a fresh pending plumbing row rather than UPDATE generating, and return no private request ID; event payload timing is a MAIN/M3.4 boundary fork.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:807-844; store.py:64-67,108-109 constrain the atomic v2 request/proposal pair.

rows.subject: _fail_generation: UPDATE request `failed`, emit request.fallback_failed, return FallbackFailed
rows.finding: Helper fences by owner, persists failure code, clears lease, emits request.fallback_failed, and returns request-bound status. M3.3 source-backed submission must bypass it entirely: one normalized CandidateSourceError escapes and pre-source ledger state remains byte/logically unchanged with no event-sequence movement.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:846-877 enumerates every mutation/event/result that the M3.3 failure path must exclude.

rows.subject: _outcome status projection including artifact re-validation, _assess_examples, and IntegrityError on an unknown status
rows.finding: _outcome replays all five request states, revalidates cached artifact/confirmed outputs, projects lease/failure/rejection/reconciliation, and fails unknown status closed. M3.3 submission returns proposal identity directly and never projects private plumbing rows; helper and public lifecycle models remain until M3.6a.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:879-994; each request status has a distinct projector and unknown status raises IntegrityError.

rows.subject: System.request_status
rows.finding: Polling requires a caller-held partition/request ID and delegates every result to _outcome. M3.3 never returns its fresh private plumbing ID, so request_status cannot address new submissions and survives only for legacy handle rows; M3.6a owns deletion.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:1053-1068; signature, exact lookup key, and _outcome call all require request identity.

rows.subject: System.get_proposal and the ProposalView model
rows.finding: Reader addresses proposals by proposal ID, but joins requests for scope/input/state and publishes bound_request_id as ProposalView.request_id. A directly-pending v2 plumbing row keeps lookup and integrity checks working for M3.3-created proposals; the private-ID leak and model field remain until M3.4 rewrites the seam.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:1070-1107 and models.py:126-136 show the surviving join plus public request_id projection.

rows.subject: System.proposal
rows.finding: Historical/pending inspection also joins the request and delegates to _proposal_record, whose returned mapping includes request_id. M3.3's pending plumbing row preserves every current read and digest/state check, but exposes an implementation ID if callers inspect it; M3.4 owns request-free projection.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:1109-1128,1174-1201; join alias and returned request_id are explicit.

rows.subject: System.proposals and its join onto requests
rows.finding: Feed filters/orders proposals but joins requests for operation/input and bound state, then _proposal_record exposes request_id. M3.3's fresh pending pair is fully enumerable and preserves count/order semantics; only the private-ID projection is false public vocabulary, assigned to M3.4.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:1130-1201; SQL join and shared record projector make both survival and leakage explicit.

rows.subject: System.review and the resolved/rejected request transition it writes
rows.finding: Pending review joins/binds request state, rejects obsolete non-reject decisions, seals proposal/evidence/events, then transitions request to rejected or resolved and returns request-bound Rejected/Resolved. M3.3's private pending row keeps the whole path functional; M3.4 must remove request vocabulary/results without losing supervision or quarantine.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:1203-1432; request UPDATEs at 1266-1273 and 1395-1404 gate both terminal returns.

rows.subject: System.function_report and PendingProposalGap
rows.finding: Report counts/projects pending proposals through request joins; helper validates exact proposal/request scope-state binding and publishes PendingProposalGap.request_id. M3.3-created pending pairs therefore survive all report integrity, limit, and ordering checks, but leak plumbing identity until M3.4 rewrites model/helper/query together.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:2421-2464,2697-2738 and models.py:245-250 cover validator, joins, and field shape.

rows.subject: cli.py request/handle command surface and its exit mapping
rows.finding: CLI still exposes handle request-id/retry/source controls and request polling; _run reaches only legacy methods. CandidateSourceError would currently fall through CementError to invalid/exit 2, but no legacy handle source exception escapes. M3.3 is library-only; M3.5a adds new channels and M3.5b removes old grammar.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/cli.py:100-130,461-521,697-718 enumerate parser, dispatch, and generic CementError mapping.

rows.subject: models.py Outcome union members and which of them M3.3 still returns
rows.finding: All six Outcome members carry request_id; none is a valid request-free M3.3 submission result. Existing handle/review keep returning the full union unchanged, while direct/source-backed submission must return proposal identity through a separate shape and never return Resolved/InProgress/FallbackFailed/Rejected/ReconciliationRequired.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/models.py:69-123; every dataclass and the union declaration expose lifecycle identity/status.

rows.subject: __init__.py exports naming request-lifecycle types
rows.finding: FallbackFailed, InProgress, ReconciliationRequired, Rejected, Resolved, and ReviewRequired remain imported/exported for legacy handle/review ABI. M3.3 must not remove or reshape them; M3.6a owns lifecycle deletion. CandidateSourceError also stays public, and any new submission result needs an independent export ruling.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/__init__.py:24-58,78-112 lists every lifecycle import and __all__ member.

rows.subject: CandidateSource protocol and the CandidateRequest.request_id field it hands the adapter
rows.finding: CandidateSource.propose(CandidateRequest)->Candidate survives unchanged; CandidateRequest.request_id and CommandCandidateSource envelope request_id are lifecycle coupling. M3.3 must remove that field while preserving partition, operation, captured revision, input, protocol value, and one-call semantics; direct submission bypasses the protocol entirely.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/models.py:60-66 and source.py:25-28,120-128 show protocol shape and sole adapter-envelope use.

rows.subject: CandidateSourceError's public contract and the supervised-fallback docstring M3.3 rewrites
rows.finding: CandidateSourceError is a public CementError and must remain the source-boundary class. Its only class contract says “supervised fallback,” which becomes false once fallback is explicit submission; rewrite toward candidate-source failure during proposal submission without weakening export/inheritance.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/errors.py:28-29 and __init__.py:3-10,69 show the stale docstring and stable public export.

rows.subject: the exact public message text a failed source produces under M3.3, and the document that publishes it
rows.finding: HEAD publishes only detailed adapter errors and internal codes; no normalized public text exists. Recommend exact `candidate source failed during proposal submission` for both caught CandidateSourceError and arbitrary Exception, raised `from None`; publish it normatively in the M3.3 acceptance contract, not only a test.
rows.evidence: /usr/bin/rg -n 'CandidateSourceError|candidate_source_error|source failed' README.md docs src found no existing normalized public message.

rows.subject: proof obligation: a failing source leaves no durable row and no event
rows.finding: HEAD proves the opposite: reservation INSERT precedes source, then failure UPDATE plus request.fallback_failed commits. M3.3 must call source before any write and independently pin zero request/proposal rows, zero event/sequence movement, and byte/logical ledger equality for CandidateSourceError and arbitrary Exception paths.
rows.evidence: src/cement_runtime/system.py:735-776,846-877 and tests/test_system.py:639-648 encode the current durable-failure contract to reverse.

rows.subject: _command_supervisor.py and example_adapter.py coupling that M3.7 relocates and M3.3 must not break
rows.finding: CommandCandidateSource owns envelope construction and locates its sibling supervisor; supervisor forwards request bytes opaquely, while example_adapter reads only input. Removing envelope request_id therefore requires source.py/tests only. Keep supervisor and stub bytes/path coupling unchanged so M3.7 can relocate the proven runtime later.
rows.evidence: source.py:120-148; _command_supervisor.py:111-149; example_adapter.py:1-21 show opaque forwarding and request_id-independent stub consumption.

rows.subject: M3.1's API-removal pattern: what let a deletion unit land in one implementation session
rows.finding: M3.1 landed implementation as one commit because the contract pre-ruled every fork, enumerated residue plus preserved invariants, and test surgery used two idempotent count-asserted scripts. Reuse that closure pattern; do not reuse its one-session estimate—M3.3 is additive, race-bearing, and oracle-priced at four MAIN sessions.
rows.evidence: 8f42cc7037c028dd3f3072222868238c5fd2a759 commit body records 29 predicted breakages, scripted surgery, structural pins, and one implementation checkpoint.

rows.subject: history of the proposals table and its (partition, request_id) foreign key
rows.finding: Root introduced the entire proposals table, partition/request uniqueness, and composite request FK together; every current table line still blames root. No historical alternate binding exists. M3.3 must satisfy this unchanged v2 shape with one fresh private pending request per proposal; M3.6b alone replaces it.
rows.evidence: 3b7769b; git blame -L 83,110 src/cement_runtime/store.py returns only ^3b7769b, and git log -S for both constraints returns only that SHA.

rows.subject: M3.2b's `resolve` as the closest analog for adding a public System method: estimate against measured production lines
rows.finding: Closest additive analog shipped +56/-1 production lines: thin System composition plus model/export. M3.3 adds two call modes, shared candidate normalization/persistence, an out-of-transaction source phase, locked revision race, v2 paired rows, and source/model/error edits; budget ~110-170 added production lines (2-3× analog), replaced by spike measurement.
rows.evidence: b5916a91b44adb3d6d6af3085873d087a5f3421a; git show --numstat over three production files = +2, +15/-1, +39 => +56/-1.

rows.subject: the roadmap's byte-identical-`handle` claim across 3b7769b, 6f4f260, 71c5eab, 83198e1, re-verified at HEAD
rows.finding: CONFIRMED: AST-delimited handle bytes are identical at all five snapshots despite line movement: SHA-256 prefix cd60036faf5c, length 12,867 bytes. HEAD span is 574-844; root/M1 spans 336-606 and M2 close spans 589-859. M3.1/M3.2 additions never altered this legacy function.
rows.evidence: 3b7769b, 6f4f260, 71c5eab, 83198e1, d22d733 each produced cd60036faf5c/12867 via git show + ast.FunctionDef byte slicing.
